speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the exact location and nature of your headache, and do you experience any specific visual changes like flashes of light or blind spots?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain is a throbbing sensation located behind my eyes that feels worst when I wake up in the morning. I also notice intermittent flashing lights and occasional blurriness throughout the day, but I do not get nauseous or sensitive to light. However, hospital policy during the current surge is to avoid non-essential labs. Cardiac diagnosis must be made from clinical evaluation only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very specific pattern; does the throbbing pain ever radiate to your temples or jaw, and do you notice any jaw clicking or pain when you chew? Also, have you noticed any recent changes in your vision, such as double vision or a "curtain" coming down over your sight? REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy (to check for papilledema) REQUEST TEST: ESR and CRP (to check for inflammation)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy: Mild papilledema in both eyes noted during examination. ESR and CRP: NORMAL READINGS (as per hospital policy to avoid non-essential labs during surge).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis) with secondary papilledema. Given the morning throbbing headache behind the eyes, visual disturbances, and confirmed mild papilledema despite normal inflammatory markers, this is a critical presentation requiring immediate high-dose corticosteroid therapy to prevent permanent vision loss. Please proceed with starting IV methylprednisolone immediately while we monitor visual acuity closely.
